verdict.reasoning: Patient states primary complaint as pain on urination: 'It hurts when I pee.' Duration confirmed: 'Uh, six days.'
Patient reports pain with urination and foul smell: 'I've got this thing when I pee, and it hurts when I go to the loo, and I've got this very unpleasant smell that comes out.'
'Pain in my tummy... In my lower tummy... In the middle.' corresponds to suprapubic pain; severity and intermittency: 'Seven... Comes and goes.'
Patient reports visible blood: 'I've had spotted, uh, blood in my urine. Spots.'

Denies fever and back/loin pain: 'No, not at all' to fever; 'you said you didn't have any lower back pain?' and 'no loin pain as well.' She states she can pass urine: 'Yes' to 'have you actually been able to pass water OK?' so no urinary retention.

First episode: 'Have you had these symptoms before?' 'No.' and 'Have you had any problems with your kidneys, or any urine infections?' answered only with 'I had IBS before,' implying no prior UTIs mentioned.
No discharge, regular menses: 'any other symptoms, any vaginal discharge or, anything like that?' Patient: 'No, just the blood spot'; 'Do you have regular periods?' Patient: 'Yes I do.'
IBS history: 'Have you had any problems with your kidneys, or any urine infections?' Patient: 'I had IBS before.'
Mebeverine regimen: 'Do you take that regularly?' 'Yes.' 'And it, do you take it three times a day?' 'Yes I do.' 'Two hundred milligrams?' 'Yes.'
Allergy documented: 'Any allergies?' ... Patient: 'Clindamycin.' Doctor: 'You're allergic to Clindamycin, OK.'
No significant family history: 'And anyone in your family had any medical problems?' Patient: 'No.'
Living situation: 'And whereabouts, do you live? Do you live with friends, family?' Patient: 'I live with friends.'
Occupation: 'And where do you work? What's your job?' Patient: 'I'm a support worker.'
Alcohol and smoking: 'Do you drink alcohol at all?' 'Occasionally.' 'So how much in a average week?' 'One glass of wine a week.' 'And do you smoke?' 'No.'
Dysuria, hematuria, suprapubic pain are all reported, and doctor states: 'it sounds very much like you, might have an infection in your urine.' This is consistent with an uncomplicated lower UTI.

Transcript confirms IBS and Mebeverine use but does not state IBS is 'stable' or discuss current IBS symptom control: 'I had IBS before.' 'I've had Mebeverine... Do you take that regularly? Yes.' No comment on stability.

Antibiotic plan and pharmacy: 'we can treat this infection... with a course of antibiotics.' 'It would just be for three days.' Prescription destination: 'the antibiotics, that I'm gonna prescribe, um, will go through to that, pharmacy.' after confirming 'Knightsbridge, Practice.'
Hydration advice: 'drink, lots of water. So, two and a half to three litres a day.'
Additional measures: 'you can get some cranberry juice and take, drink that as well' and 'some, sachets... which just help change the acidity of your urine.'
Thermometer advice: 'Have you got a thermometer at home?' 'No.' 'It would be helpful if you could get a thermometer from the pharmacy and, do check your temperature.'

Safety-netting: 'if you feel like your pain is getting worse or not settling, you get lower back pain, um, or you're getting a high temperature, or you have any problems actually passing urine. Then it's very important that we speak to you again.' and advice about recurrent problems needing further discussion.
Transcript confirms current Mebeverine regimen but there is no explicit instruction to 'continue' Mebeverine as part of this visit's plan.

Follow-up as needed: 'if you feel like your symptoms get worse at any point, or they're not resolving with the treatment... then it's important for us to talk, talk to you in more detail about that.' and 'No, not if you're better' when asked about routine follow-up.
